advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or soften the body prose-string greps in test_prompt_contract_front_matter (lines 84-85), keeping only the structural front-matter/prompt_id assertions, so the test does not break on a behavior-preserving rubric reword.
evidence: assert "ADVISORY" in body and "does NOT block" in body
assert "LAYER-CAKE" in body and "CONSUMED-ARTIFACT-WITHOUT-ORDERING-EDGE" in body

The grepped tokens are free-prose rubric content read only by the LLM finder (not parsed by a validator/loader), unlike the front-matter keys parsed by the prompt loader — an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so these are wording-guarding change-detectors.
advisory.finding: test_prompt_contract_front_matter greps prose strings ('ADVISORY', 'does NOT block', 'LAYER-CAKE', 'CONSUMED-ARTIFACT-WITHOUT-ORDERING-EDGE') from the reviewer rubric .md body; these guard authorial wording whose only consumer is the LLM, so they act as change-detectors that break on a behavior-preserving reword of the rubric rather than verifying an observable contract. The front-matter KEY assertions (execution_mode/dimension/category, prompt_id) in the same test ARE structural and valid.
scenarios: A future reword of the rubric prose (e.g. 'layer-cake' lowercased, or 'never blocks' instead of 'does NOT block') that preserves the criterion's behavior would fail the test with no behavior change.
